newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal down on hog population projections.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal down on hog population projections.

text.p: CBOT soybean meal futures were lower at midsession, as traders sold futures in anticipation of a drop in feed demand from the hog industry, traders said.
The U.S. Agriculture Department on Friday reported that the total number of hogs in the U.S. was 96 percent of the year-ago level, versus an average trade estimate of 98.4 percent.

Soyoil futures were also mostly lower, as that market fell in tandem with soybeans. Losses in soyoil were limited by talk that China was still actively making inquiries in South American export markets. Last week China bought 26,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil.
"China is definitely still in the (soyoil) market," said one trader with ties to the cash market.

Losses in the soymeal market were trimmed by heavy commercial buying, floor sources said. Continental Grain bought 300 lots January and 100 lots of March, and Term Commodities bought 400 lots of March, floor sources said.
At 1152 CST, soymeal was down $1.00 to $2.40 per ton, with January down $2.40 at $228.50. Soyoil was up 0.05 cent per pound to down 0.07, with January down 0.05 at 22.81.
